one_liner: Header-only C++17 JSON codec for structs with compile-time-known shape; README claims up to 9x nlohmann/json, 2x RapidJSON.
what_it_does: Encodes and decodes C++ structs, std::vector, std::tuple, std::optional, std::variant and iod metamaps directly to and from JSON text, with no DOM in between. You declare each field name once with the IOD_SYMBOL macro, describe the shape with json_object(s::age, s::name) or json_vector(...), then call .encode(obj) or .decode(str, obj); plain vectors, tuples and metamaps also work through json_encode/json_decode. It is not a drop-in for nlohmann/json or RapidJSON: there is no dynamic value type, and decode returns a json_error instead of throwing.
how_it_is_fast: The schema is a compile-time template expression (one type per symbol, plus metamaps), so the decoder writes each value straight into the target member and the encoder walks the fields without building a tree; key lookup is a linear strncmp over the schema's members. Input is read through a pointer-bumping decode_stringstream over a string_view, and numbers use hand-rolled digit-accumulation parsers (integer part, fractional part divided by a power of ten, power-of-ten exponent) instead of strtod. Part of the gap to the baselines is work it skips: no buffer-end checks, no correctly rounded float parsing, and no skipping of unknown keys.
when_to_use: Studying the compile-time-schema, no-DOM decoding idea in about 1,200 lines before adopting its maintained continuation, li::json in matt-42/lithium.
Decoding small, trusted, fixed-shape messages that your own code produces (a few int/string fields, flat int or float arrays) where every key is known in advance.
Older GCC 7/8 C++17 codebases that already use iod symbols and metamaps and want struct binding without a DOM.
Binaries that must stay small for a handful of message types: the README claims up to 8x smaller code than nlohmann/json, measured on one float-array decoder (issue #1).
when_not_to_use: Untrusted input. At HEAD, decode_stringstream never checks the buffer end, so truncated input or an unterminated string reads past the buffer. Keys of 50 or more characters write one byte past a 50-byte stack buffer, and decoding into std::string_view loops forever on any backslash. lithium fixed these in 2026; metajson never got the fixes.

Numbers you need exactly. Values between -1 and 0 decode as positive (-0.5 becomes 0.5), and li::json still has the same sign logic. The integer part of a float is parsed into an int and overflows past about 2.1e9. Exponents or fractional-digit counts of 18 or more hit a zero power of ten (1.5e-20 gives inf, 1e20 gives 0). '1e+5' is rejected. Floats are encoded with the default 6-digit ostream precision.

JSON from other producers or evolving schemas. Any key not in the schema fails the whole decode ('Unknown json key'). There is no true/false/null support (bool is written and read as 1/0). std::variant uses a custom {"idx":N,"value":...} wrapper, and std::map is not supported (issue #9, still open).
Dynamic or schema-less documents such as config files or arbitrary API payloads: there is no DOM or generic value type at all.
Current libc++ toolchains (Apple Clang, recent LLVM): the headers include <experimental/tuple>, which libc++ no longer ships, and nobody has maintained the code since 2019.

integration.dependencies: The single header libraries/metajson/metajson.hh (last regenerated 2018-07) needs only the standard library. The modular headers at HEAD need the iod/symbol and iod/metamap headers from iodcpp/iod. The benchmarks need Google Benchmark, RapidJSON and nlohmann/json.
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (-std=c++1z). The README lists GCC 7.1.1 and Clang 5.0.1. The code needs <experimental/tuple> (std::experimental::apply), which libstdc++ still ships and current libc++ does not. MSVC is not documented.
integration.platforms: any (README: no architecture-specific code). Input must be a contiguous buffer (std::string, string_view or const char*); std::istream input is not supported.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Parser and encoder state is per call and the headers hold no mutable globals, so concurrent calls on different objects look safe.

gotchas: Encoding copies: json_object_base::encode(O obj) and impl::json_encode(C&, O obj, ...) take the object by value, so every encode copies the struct, including each element of a vector of structs. Every std::string is also copied into a std::stringstream before escaping.

make_json_error, json_no_error and detect_encoding are non-inline functions defined in the header, so including metajson in more than one .cc file of the same binary gives duplicate-symbol link errors.
Every failed decode leaks memory: the parser allocates its error std::stringstream with new and never frees it (li::json later switched to unique_ptr).

Packaging drift: the README's install URL (raw.githubusercontent.com/iodcpp/metajson/master/metajson.hh) returns 404 since the 2019 'Prepare the merge' commit moved everything under libraries/metajson/. That single header is older than the 2019 modular headers, and the repo also carries committed a.out binaries and a 52 MB nlohmann_json.hpp.gch.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: glaze and reflect-cpp handle the same typed struct-binding workload, publish multi-document benchmarks (the catalog lists about 3.7x round-trip and about 2x over RapidJSON respectively), support full JSON literals and are maintained, so prefer them for real use. Pick metajson only to read a compact compile-time-schema decoder; if you like its API, use its continuation li::json (lithium_json.hh) instead.
verified_claims_summary: The README claims up to 9x faster than nlohmann/json and 2x faster than RapidJSON, but publishes no results table, compiler or CPU. The public Google Benchmark sources (-O3 -march=native) time decoding a 3-field object and 60-element int/float arrays into C++ values, while the RapidJSON and nlohmann versions build a DOM and copy out of it; the author wrote in issue #1 that 'being fair was not the goal' and in issue #6 that nativejson-benchmark could not be implemented with metajson.
status_note: Abandoned since 2019-11-26 and MIT-licensed; the code moved into matt-42/lithium as li::json, which is still maintained (last push 2026-07-31) and received 2026 bounds-checking and security fixes that metajson never got, so metajson is small enough to vendor but only after you fix the parser bugs above.
